cards.text: Jeremiah the prophet has a word from the LORD, and this time it isn't for a king or a crowd. It's for one man: Baruch son of Neriah. Baruch is the one helping Jeremiah get the LORD's words down.

cards.question: When this word comes, Baruch is writing Jeremiah's words down on a ___.

cards.text: Jeremiah talks and Baruch writes, word for word, in the fourth year of Jehoiakim son of Josiah, king of Judah. Baruch is basically Jeremiah's voice-to-text, except voice-to-text never gets a HAND CRAMP.

cards.question: The LORD speaks to Baruch by name and starts with Baruch's own words. How has Baruch been feeling?
Baruch says the LORD has added sorrow on top of the pain he already had.

cards.text: Baruch says he's worn out with GROANING, friend. Then Jeremiah passes along the LORD's answer, and it starts with the whole land.

cards.question: Throughout the land, the LORD says He will demolish and uproot. Whose work is coming down?

answers.text: What He Himself built and planted
What the kings of Judah built and planted

cards.text: Then the LORD turns from the whole land right back to Baruch. He has a question, and it's about what Baruch has been reaching for.

cards.question: The LORD asks Baruch about what he's reaching for. What does He ask if Baruch is seeking?
The LORD tells Baruch to keep reaching for great things for himself.

cards.text: Instead, the LORD gives Baruch two words: "Stop seeking!" No speech, no slideshow, no follow-up email, friend, just STOP.

cards.question: Next the LORD says He will bring disaster. What will it fall on?
But wherever Baruch goes, the LORD will grant him his ___ as a spoil of war.

findings.problem: The first sentence, "Baruch says he's worn out with GROANING, friend," repeats Jeremiah 45:3, which cards 4 and 5 already asked and answered. Only the second sentence moves the passage forward to verse 4. Drop the recap and spend the card on the turn to the LORD's answer.

The card says the LORD gives "No speech, no slideshow, no follow-up email... just STOP." But Jeremiah 45:5 goes on right after "Stop seeking!" with a reason: "For I will bring disaster on every living creature..." and then a promise to Baruch. The joke says the text has no follow-up when it does. The joke also lands on the LORD's own words, which comes close to aiming the humor at God.

rule.text: Papa Dorin can retell in his own words and fill in what the text clearly implies. Scene-setting details are fine. He never says anything the text shows is wrong.

findings.problem: The joke's target is the way the LORD speaks in Jeremiah 45:5. That is close to humor aimed at God rather than at Papa Dorin or at a human situation.

rule.text: His humor never targets God, Jesus, Scripture or the Marriage Supper.

findings.problem: The walkthrough has only two real jokes, on cards 3 and 11, and card 11's joke has to be reworked. Cards 1, 6 and 8 read as pleasant narration with no laugh, even though the passage gives openings that don't touch any facts. For example, Papa Dorin could relate to being worn out and getting no rest from his drawer days, or poke fun at himself about reaching for great things.

rule.text: When a moment can hold a real laugh without muddying a fact, he goes for it. If a line reads like a nice dad being pleasant, push it further.
